**Direct answer: no one has. No human has ever walked on Mars, so the question rests on a false premise.** Only uncrewed robotic craft have operated on the surface.

**Claims and sources**

- No human has landed on or walked on Mars. NASA's Mars page lists the planet's population as "zero" and calls it a planet inhabited entirely by robots.
  https://www.nasa.gov/humans-in-space/humans-to-mars/

- Crewed Mars missions are still in development. NASA is working on power, life support, spacesuits, communications and habitats.
  https://www.nasa.gov/humans-in-space/humans-to-mars/

- NASA's stated goal is to send astronauts to Mars "as early as the 2030s", and it uses a 2039 roundtrip as an example. The page says it is being updated for recent Artemis program changes, so these dates may shift.
  https://www.nasa.gov/humans-in-space/humans-to-mars/

- The closest thing to "Mars crews" so far is Earth-based simulation. NASA's first CHAPEA crew finished a 378-day simulated Mars surface mission at Johnson Space Center. It began June 25, 2023, and the crew left the habitat on July 6.
  https://www.nasa.gov/missions/analog-field-testing/chapea/first-mars-crew-completes-yearlong-simulated-red-planet-nasa-mission/

**Caveats**

- I read one page in full, NASA's Mars page. The CHAPEA claim comes from a search-result snippet, and I didn't open that page.
- The NASA page doesn't state outright that nobody has landed on Mars. That part is inferred from the "zero" population line and the "still in development" wording.
- One search result (theopenknowledge.com) claimed a NASA crew was named for a 2028 Mars mission. It conflicts with NASA's own page and looks unreliable, so I disregarded it.
- I used two source retrievals, one search and one page read.

Sources:
- [NASA: Humans to Mars](https://www.nasa.gov/humans-in-space/humans-to-mars/)
- [NASA: First Mars Crew Completes Yearlong Simulated Red Planet Mission](https://www.nasa.gov/missions/analog-field-testing/chapea/first-mars-crew-completes-yearlong-simulated-red-planet-nasa-mission/)
